checks: The first variation over all nonvertical normal parameters is feasible before positive normalization. The width derivative is the covariance-norm differential and the fixed mark buffer does not vary. Using m_0=hq−b(Y) gives the two stated moment equations with the correct sign of A.

Every fixed normal tail is continuous and nonincreasing. At an attaining positive-strip threshold its derivative is negative, excluding any other threshold of the same mass. The right-quantile inequalities are convex on the hull because b is concave. A pure-base cap containing a convex combination contains at least one positive-weight input, and a parallel cap through that input is contained in it. Thus integer-base combinations of deepest marks are deepest.

Equality in the weighted quantile inequalities fixes exactly the same geometric cap, positive S, and moments at all inputs. Its base moment makes their bases coincide. The strip barycenter Z is in C at that base and has A/S<0 because the uniform ramp derivative is supported on the open negative strip and S>0.

The continuous moments put every input at Z+t∇Γ(u) with t=b(Y)−A/S>0 and b(Y)=t+A/S. If 0<t_1<t_2, concavity at the first point between Z and the second yields (1−t_1/t_2)b(Z)≤(1−t_1/t_2)A/S. This contradicts b(Z)≥0. The factor is positive, and no strict concavity of b or compact active set is needed.

Source 0fa64553cd01d7ae §3 gives the same cap moments and integer-base argument, and 6e754f2bf13bdbd1 §2 provides the zero-buffer singleton case. The revised strip argument proves the broader same-base claim. Singleton fibers, empty lattice hull, and distinct occupied parities follow from the no-combination result.
